  "situation": "By spring 1942, several U.S. agencies, including the State Department, FBI, and FCC, had begun their own communications-intelligence activities alongside the Army and Navy. Military authorities sought a high-level decision limiting governmental activity in cryptanalysis, and the Joint Chiefs of Staff served as the forum for adjudicating intelligence responsibilities. An interdepartmental committee with Army, Navy, and FBI members surveyed cryptanalytic responsibilities and met on 30 June 1942. Its agreement confined cryptanalytic activity to the Army, Navy, and FBI and established wartime dissemination policy. On 6 July, the Joint Chiefs reported the agreement to the President and recommended excluding other U.S. agencies from the field.",
